Mean pairwise cosine measures average angular alignment, not information loss. A common mean direction can produce high similarity while informative residual dimensions remain; balanced vectors along ±one axis can have near-zero mean cosine despite rank-one collapse. Cosine also ignores norms. Thus, anisotropy alone does not establish collapse or poor recommendation quality; useful representations can be anisotropic. [Ethayarajh, 2019](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.00512)

Inspect centered covariance eigenvalues, total variance, leading-eigenvalue share, and effective rank together. Define covariance effective rank explicitly as exp(−Σ pᵢ log pᵢ), pᵢ=λᵢ/Σλᵢ; RankMe instead normalizes embedding singular values, giving a different statistic. Concentrated spectra indicate dimensional restriction; near-zero total variance indicates nearly constant representations. Effective rank is invariant to uniform scaling, so it cannot detect uniformly vanishing variance by itself; handle zero variance explicitly. Report embedding-norm distributions and compare raw versus unit-normalized spectra to separate magnitude variation from directional structure. High rank can also reflect noise, so it does not guarantee useful ranking. [Dimensional collapse](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.09348), [RankMe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02885)

For diagnostics, the algebraic implication is straightforward: multiplying scores by any positive constant enlarges raw positive-minus-negative margins without changing rankings. Dot-product margins therefore mix separation with embedding norms and temperature. Report pairwise accuracy, P(s⁺>s⁻), with half-credit for ties, alongside margins and score/norm distributions. Accuracy survives strictly increasing score transformations, but depends on negative difficulty and sampling; easy negatives can conceal poor top-10 retrieval. Use fixed pairs across comparisons, exclude padding, diagnose item embeddings and final nonpadding history features separately, and retain pinned validation HR@10 as the selection criterion.
